messages.author: a59df4914e45df44
messages.subject: Callrate Plot
parts:
Hello everyone, 

Hopefully this question has a simple/straightforward answer. When filtering a relatively large (90k) SNP data set using gl.filter.callrate, I receive a callrate histogram with a weird gap (image attached). Has anyone seen something similar? It seems too weird to be explained by a random process. 

Thank you,
Mike Sandel

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Callrate Plot
parts:
Hi Mike,

I think the problem might be due to the number of bins used in the plot. In the developing version of dartR, we have added the option to change the number of bins. You can install this version if you follow the code below.

My suggestion would be to try with different number of bins and check if you still get the same weird results.

Please let us know whether this worked for you.

library(devtools)
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")

res_1 <- gl.filter.callrate(bandicoot.gl,method= "ind",threshold = 0.85, bins = 30)
res_2 <- gl.filter.callrate(bandicoot.gl,method= "ind",threshold = 0.85, bins = 10)

Cheers,
Luis
